235_prologue_content.text: Have you ever secretly admired someone? Admired their good looks. Admired their talents. Admired how cute they are. Anything that leads you to seek out and find out what they look like or what they do. Especially nowadays, in the age of social media, which makes it much easier for people to secretly admire someone.
If you have experienced this feeling, then you are like

, the popular girl in school, without even expecting to exist in her eyes. Just feeling happy scrolling through her phone and seeing her face. Ongsa would never have dared to think that there would be a day when the 23.5-degree tilt of the Earth's axis could bring her closer to the
Questioning whether what she felt was simple “admiration” or not.

, Yuri's second work published by everY. It's not often that we come across this kind of work, but when we do, it's guaranteed to be fun. We should also start this by saying that this story is so beautiful (as much as a long trip to Neptune). A story about an innocent love in the turbulent teenage years that will make you smile as you read from the first page to the last page.

235_intro_content.text: The innocent, naive one is always the victim.
After turning around and not seeing the person mentioned, she turns her head back to her meatball vanishing as if getting stolen.
- "Tinh, did you take my meatball again? Damn you! Spit it out."
- "Ouch, ouch, Ongsa, don't strangle me. Cough, cough."
-- The only boy in the group cries for help.
- "Charoen, you trashy friend. Ongsa, I can't breathe. Cough, cough."
A slender female student is strangling a chubby male student with another female student laughing at the side. It might look like a violent scene, but it's common for these kids.
three best friends, have been close since middle school. Now that they're in the tenth grade, they're still from the same class.
The two dear friends laugh at their best friend's silliness.
Ongsa wasn't usually easily fooled. The thing is, today, she hasn't seen someone's face since morning.
... this name has a particular impact on Ongsa. Sun is in the tenth grade, the same as her.
The truth is, Ongsa knows Sun, but she's not sure if Sun knows her.
... Ongsa has a crush on her...
The feelings were so strong that her gang began to notice.

But no matter how strong the feelings are, Ongsa can't express them. She's a shy person. She doesn't have that much courage. More importantly, Ongsa is a girl. How can she ever say things like that when Sun...

235_chapter1_title: A Coincidence / A Small World / Destiny

235_chapter1_content.text: Starting a new semester with complaints, then getting bored out of your mind during the summer break, is perfectly normal for middle schoolers. Ongsa is one of them.
When you're drowning in piles of schoolwork, only to suddenly have way too much free time during the break, it's hard to adjust.
Another reason this summer break feels more tedious than usual to Ongsa is that she has just been dumped.
Well, “dumped” isn't exactly accurate. It's more like she was forced to accept the truth that...
...Some good people are better off as friends, not lovers...

Usually, Ongsa gets sent to cram school during summer break, so she hardly ever has enough free time to get bored. But this is the break before tenth grade, and she has loads of things to prepare for.
Submitting documents.
Preparatory courses.
Other preparations.
Yada, yada, yada.

That's why her family decided not to send her to cram school this summer. At first, Ongsa was happy that she could finally take a break instead of studying right away. She never expected staying home to be this boring.
And this is only the first week.
“I'm boooooooooooooored!!!”
She's home alone, so she can yell as loudly as she wants.
“Woof!”
Actually, she's not exactly alone.
“What's wrong, Latte?”
“Woof!!”
She's alone with another creature, that's all.
“Woof woof!!”
“I didn't want to yell. I was just bored.”
“Woof!!”
“Would you stop complaining? Keep barking and I'll eat you!”
That's right. This is Ongsa's talent...
She can have conversations with dogs.
“Wow, Gam's school just held its graduation ceremony? That's late.”
Ongsa isn't usually much of a talker, but for some reason, she talks a lot when she's alone.
“She uploaded a ton of photos to Instagram. It's practically an exhibition.”
Like other ninth graders, Gam—Ongsa's childhood friend from primary school, who attends a different school—has posted photos from her graduation day on Instagram, the popular social media app.
Ongsa scrolls through her feed, grumbling to her dog, until she comes across one particular photo.
...A group photo...
At first glance, it looks like any ordinary middle school graduation group photo. But to Ongsa, who's mindlessly scrolling through her feed, there's one noticeable difference.
Instead of looking like a group of friends posing together, the people in the photo seem to be surrounding one person.
When Ongsa reads the caption below...
“A photo with the most famous girl in our grade. #excited”
Ongsa assumes the girl in the center must be someone popular in her grade. Maybe Gam's friend asked to take a photo with her.
“She's cute, isn't she, Latte?”
“Woof!!”
“Right? I think so too. Oh! Gam tagged her. Let me take a look.”
“Woof!”
“What? I'm only taking a quick look. See? She's super cute!”
At last, Ongsa has found something to do on this long, boring day.
That something is snooping around a stranger's Instagram account.
And it ends with her following the account...
“Ongsa, go upstairs and get Alpha.”
“Why don't you call her yourself? Why do I have to go up there?”
“I texted your sister before we left, and she said her phone was about to die. I called her earlier, but she didn't answer, so I guess the battery's dead. Go get her so she'll know where we parked.”
“Send Latte up instead,” Ongsa bargains.
“Then I'll give your dog's allowance to him.”
“Ugggh, Dad! Fine, I'll go!”
Defeated, Ongsa gets out of the car as her father orders.
The family is having dinner at her grandfather's house today. Ongsa and her father have driven out with Latte to pick up her older sister from cram school before heading to Grandpa's place together.
Ongsa drags her feet toward the elevator. During summer break, every fiber of her body seems cursed with laziness.
Why didn't Dad ask Latte to go get Alpha? All he has to do is call her down. A genius dog like Latte could definitely handle that mission.
Alpha's classroom is on the seventh floor. Ongsa remembers it well because she usually waits there for her sister after class so they can go home together.
Now that she thinks about it, coming to cram school without having to study actually feels great. It's like she's been set free.
Ongsa steps into the elevator to go to the seventh floor and get her sister. Just as the doors are about to close, she spots someone running toward them from a distance.
Since she's in no hurry, Ongsa holds the elevator door open for the person.
“Thank you!”
The girl thanks her, panting after running to the elevator.
Ongsa returns her smile, since she's not very good at talking to strangers. But when she gets a clear look at the girl's face...
For a moment, the world seems to stop spinning.
...This person...
By the time Ongsa comes to her senses, the elevator doors have opened on the fifth floor. The girl steps out, but turns back to smile at Ongsa one more time before leaving.
...She's freaking cute...
Ongsa keeps staring at the girl until the elevator doors close.
Have you ever felt this way?

You recognize someone because you see them every day on social media. You know what they do, know about their daily activities, and even feel as if you're close to them. But when you meet them in real life, you can't even say hello, no matter how much you want to.
You know them...
But they don't know you.
After that day, Ongsa starts seriously looking through the girl's Instagram account. She checks every photo, reads every caption, and gathers quite a bit more information.
Her name is Sun.
They're the same age.
She likes cats.
And she's unbelievably, ridiculously cute ><

It's a lot like becoming a fan of an artist. Once you fall for them, you want to learn more about them. The more you learn, the more you like them. And when you finally meet them, you just want to see them again.
Ongsa is just like that.

She doesn't understand why she's suddenly feeling this way about someone her own age. To Ongsa, it's simple: Sun is just too cute. Sun's photos always put her in a good mood, and their encounter that day made her realize one thing...
Sun is a hundred times cuter in real life than in photos!
Actually, Ongsa has tried visiting the cram school several times, hoping to run into Sun again. But they still haven't crossed paths.
Well, coincidences don't happen that easily...
“Ongsaaaaaaa!”
“Oh, Tinh! Hi. You're early.”
“Don't ‘hi’ me! You jerk! You didn't take the preparatory courses, and neither did that damn Charoen. Neither of you showed up anywhere. You both abandoned meeeee!”

“Sorry, sorry. My relatives suddenly got together and went on a trip, and my family joined them on a whim. By the time we got back, there was only one week of break left. I really couldn't be bothered to study anymore. Didn't I text you? Why did you go?”

“Easy for you to say! Where else was I supposed to go? Dad drove me straight to the school gate. If he could, he'd probably carry me all the way to the classroom. Where else could I possibly go? You were having fun with your family, while Charoen basically disappeared. I didn't even know whether she was enjoying her break or had died somewhere! I couldn't contact her. There are only three of us in this whole school. Who else am I supposed to hang out with, you little jerk Ongsa? Answer meeeee!”
A short question gets a ridiculously long answer, as if Tinh has been waiting ages to tell the whole story and complain.
“Ongsa, Tinh!”
Speak of the devil. The last member of their little gang has finally arrived.
“Charooooooooen! Are you alive or dead?!”
“Wow... Screw you. Is that really how you greet me?” Charoen asks Tinh.
“Yes, especially you! I couldn't contact you all summer, and you weren't active on social media either. I thought you'd vanished from the face of the earth!”
“Right. You didn't reply to my messages either,” Ongsa chimes in.
“I went on a pilgrimage to the border with my grandpa. He's a monk.”
“Huuuuuh?!!” both friends cry out in shock.
“A pilgrimage?” Ongsa repeats, making sure she heard correctly.
“Yeah.”
“But you're a girl. Why would your grandpa let you go with him?” Tinh asks.
They both know Charoen's grandfather became a monk long before she was born, and that he's an extremely strict monk. How could he have allowed his granddaughter to go on a pilgrimage with him?
“Actually, I didn't go with my grandpa. I went with my dad.”
“Here's what happened: my family didn't want Grandpa to go on a pilgrimage because he's getting old, but he insisted. So Dad went along to keep an eye on him from a distance.”
“And you followed your dad?” Tinh asks.
“Yeah.”
“And he let you go?” Ongsa asks.

“No. I secretly followed him and got caught by Dad in the woods. He couldn't make me go back because I didn't know the way. He also couldn't take me back himself because he was worried about Grandpa. In the end, I went on the pilgrimage with Grandpa.”
“Seriously?!!” Ongsa and Tinh exclaim together again.

“No! I made the whole thing up from the start. Are you two idiots? My grandpa is seventy. Who would let him go on a pilgrimage? Dad has a job too. He wouldn't have time to accompany Grandpa. Besides, if I'd really followed Dad into the woods like I said, he would've stomped me to death right there. You're both so easy to fool. Haha!”
“You little jeeeeeerk!! You sounded so serious that we totally fell for it! I'm an innocent, naive person. How could I ever be suspicious of you, Charoen?!”
“So where did you actually go? Tell us the truth this time,” Ongsa asks again.
“I went to practice Dharma with my grandma.”
“Is that true?”
“Yes, Tinh. I stayed at a temple in the forest for a whole month. Phones weren't allowed there, so I couldn't contact you two.”
“Oh...” At last, her two friends understand.
“Why have you buttoned your collar all the way up?” Tinh asks after looking Charoen's uniform over from top to bottom.
“It's a style.”
“Ugggh!!”
Ongsa, Tinh, and Charoen are considered the weird ones by the other students. Maybe that's why they've been close since middle school and even ended up in the same class in tenth grade.
Who knows whether it's fate sent down from heaven...
Or a curse delivered straight from hell.
DINGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGG!!!
The bell for the morning assembly rings, cutting off their conversation.
They leave their schoolbags on the bench and head to the assembly area as usual.
On the way, Ongsa's eyes land on a familiar face.
Someone she never thought she'd see here.
At this very moment...
The owner of the Instagram account Ongsa has been secretly stalking all summer...
...In a high school uniform...
...And attending the same school as her...
“WHAT?!!!”
...Coincidences rarely happen...
...but they're not as rare as you think...

235_chapter2_content.text: "What's wrong, Ongsa?"
"Nothing. Let's go to the assembly." Ongsa pretended nothing had happened, even though her heart was dancing hip-hop like crazy.

Guess how shocked Ongsa was when she saw Sun lining up near her. She was so stunned that she kept her arms crossed over her chest even after the prayer, until Charoen had to pull them down. Throughout her first day at school, Ongsa wandered around like someone who had lost her soul.
"Ongsa, what's wrong with you? You look completely spaced out. Didn't you sleep well last night?" Tinh asked worriedly.
"Yeah. I went to bed late." Ongsa casually brushed off the question without explaining anything. Not that she knew how to explain it to her friends anyway.
"You can't keep doing this. The school year has started. Fix your sleep schedule, or you're going to be in trouble," Charoen reminded her.
"Okay, I'll go to bed early tonight."

It was funny how Ongsa had suddenly become a fan of a girl around her age, only for that girl to transfer to her school. Even more ironically, despite now being so close to each other, nothing had really changed from when they attended different schools.
Still, a few things had changed. Ongsa had found Sun's Facebook and Twitter accounts, sent her a friend request, and followed her.
...That was all...
What Ongsa liked most was whenever Sun smiled.
...She was genuinely happy to see that smile from such a close distance...
"Ongsa, if we don't choose a position, they'll make us dance. What are we going to do?"
"Ongsa!!!"
"Huh?!"
"Did you even hear what Charoen asked? Good grief, you're glued to your phone every day. Is your boyfriend living in there or something? Could you look up and talk to us for once?" Tinh grumbled.
Ongsa immediately put her phone down on the table. "What?"
"I asked which position you want for Sports Day. Are you planning to dance like you did last year?" Charoen asked again.
"Nah... I'll pass. Practicing is too much work."
"Yeah, same here."
While they were discussing their options, someone walked over.
"Tinh."
"Oh... Hi, P'Pai."

Among the three friends, Charoen and Ongsa were the shy ones who hardly interacted with anyone. Tinh was the complete opposite. He was an extrovert who seemed to know almost everyone at school. The senior who had just greeted him was the head of the student council's activities committee.
"Have you chosen your position for Sports Day yet?"
"Not yet. What's up, P'Pai?"
"Could you help the student council carry the parade palanquin?"
"You want me to sit on it?"
"No, I want you to help carry it."
WARNING: WATCH YOUR STEP. SOMEONE'S PRIDE HAS JUST SHATTERED INTO PIECES.
"HAHAHAHAHA!!"
"If you don't want me to slap your teeth out, both of you had better stop laughing!"

After threatening her friends, Tinh turned back to the senior and made a scene. "P'Pai, why would you make a delicate girl like me carry a palanquin? What were you thinking? How could you be so cruel?"

"Come on, Tinh... Please help us out. We're short on people, and I don't know who else to ask. The student council has already assigned everyone to their Sports Day duties. Think of it as doing something for our school, okay?"
"Good grief... Those palanquins are heavy. Can I even carry one?"
"Of course you can. There are eight people carrying it. It's not that heavy. The girl sitting on it is tiny, after all."
"So I have to carry it with a bunch of huge guys? Can't these two help me instead?" Tinh tried to pass the responsibility to Ongsa and Charoen.
"Wow, you really think that's reasonable? We can help if we can, but Ongsa is lucky just to stay upright on two legs, and you're asking her to carry a palanquin!"

"I don't want to go alone. It'll be lonely. If I practice with a bunch of boys, they'll tease me. A fragile girl like me can't be thrown into a den of wolves all by herself. Forget it, P'Pai. If these two aren't coming with me, I'm not participating." Tinh laid down his condition.

The senior thought for a moment. There weren't many students left with free time, since each color team had already been assigned most of its duties. Besides, finding people willing to carry a palanquin was never easy.
"All right... Your friends can join the support team for the parade."
"Sure! It's a deal. I'm ready to serve!" Charoen replied cheerfully.
"Wait, Charoen... Did you even ask me first?"
"Come on, Tinh... I can see the burning desire to contribute to our school in your eyes. We'll sacrifice ourselves and accompany you, so don't worry."
"You little bastard!!!"
"All right, then. It's settled. Thank you so much, everyone. I'll be off now."
"Wait, P'Pai! Wait! Good grief! She's already gone. Nobody ever listens to me."
"Now all of us have duties for Sports Day. We're so lucky, aren't we, Ongsa?"
"Yeah ^^"
"Oh, absolutely... Lucky my ass! You're enjoying your good fortune at the expense of my misery!!!"

Actually, Tinh's palanquin duty wasn't that demanding. He only had to practice for a week before Sports Day. Ongsa and Charoen's support-team duties were much the same. So while everyone else was busy preparing, the three of them had more free time than most.
"Ongsa, I've noticed you've been using your phone a lot lately," Tinh remarked while they had nothing to do.
"That's true. Are you texting someone?" Charoen added.
"No."
"Hey... Tell us the truth. Have you gotten over it yet?"
"Gotten over what?"
"Ton."
"Tinh, you jerk..." Charoen muttered, cursing him for asking such a blunt question.
"Um... I don't feel anything anymore. Honestly, I don't think I ever really liked him in the first place," Ongsa said, speaking at unusual length about her feelings.
"Good. We're just worried about you, you know? If you've moved on, that's great. No matter what, we're still friends." Tinh patted Ongsa on the shoulder to comfort her.
It wasn't entirely true that she no longer felt anything...
Because she still had feelings...
...They just didn't hurt as much as they used to...
"Tinh, this is your position. Remember to count your steps while marching so everyone stays in sync."
At last, Sports Day was only a week away. It was that time of year when students came to school to prepare for activities instead of studying.
"Ongsa, take the water upstairs for everyone. Charoen, help me lift this."
The place was absolute chaos. Ongsa hated crowded activities like this, but at least it was better than having to dance like she did last year.
"Hey, hey."
Someone lightly tapped Ongsa on the shoulder. She turned around, nearly dropping the two buckets she was carrying.
"Do you know where the room for the student council parade participants is?"
"Sun!" Someone called before Ongsa could say anything else.
"Hi, P'Pai. I just saw you standing over there, but when I turned around, you were gone. Which room should I go to?"
"It's on the second floor. Ongsa is taking water up to everyone there. Ongsa, could you show her the way?"
"Let me help you." Sun took one of the buckets from her.
"..." The cat had stolen Ongsa's tongue.
"Let's go."
"Uh... yeah..."
...Maybe this year's Sports Day would be more fun than she had expected...
If you think joining the same Sports Day team would help Ongsa and Sun become closer, then you...
Are WRONG!!
As mentioned before, Ongsa wasn't good at socializing and didn't have many connections. So it was no surprise that she remained nothing more than a quiet fan of Sun.
Sports Day finally came to an end, and everything went back to normal.
"Ongsa."
"Hmm?"
"Do you like Sun from Grade 6?"
"What?!"
Both Ongsa and Charoen were shocked by Tinh's unexpected question. Charoen and Tinh knew Sun because she was the girl sitting on the palanquin Tinh had helped carry.
"I'm serious. I really want to know."
"Are you crazy? How could I like her? She's a girl!" Ongsa hurriedly denied it.
"So what? I'm a guy, and I like guys," Tinh replied casually.
"That's you. I'm a girl, so how could I like another girl? What a stupid question." Ongsa continued to deny it.

"Really? Before you answer, did you notice Sun's Instagram account on your phone screen? Don't think I haven't noticed you secretly checking Sun's Facebook and Instagram all day. I caught on during the summer break, but it wasn't until Sports Day preparations that I figured it out. Whenever Sun shows up, you smile so brightly you practically glow. And during Sports Day, you kept taking pictures of the girl sitting on the palanquin, even though your best friend was the one struggling to carry it. You're not subtle at all. You've got a thing for her, don't you?"
"No."
"Are you suuuure? (-O-)"
"Fine. I admit it. I like her."
"Oh my freaking God!! Ongsa, are you a lesbian?" Charoen screamed in shock.
"Good grief! Listen. I like her in an admiring kind of way. She's cute, so I'm a fan. It's not like I want her to be my girlfriend."
"Oh..." Charoen seemed to understand.
"We'll see about that." Tinh, on the other hand, still wasn't convinced.
I just like her smile. Does that mean I really like her? Ongsa wondered, keeping the question to herself.
"Let's change the subject. The student council is organizing a volunteer camp during the break. Do you two want to join? P'Pai asked me to check," Tinh said, moving on to a new topic.
"I'm going to attend extra classes at a tutoring center," Ongsa replied.
"I'm going on a pilgrimage with my grandfather."
"Charoen..." Tinh interrupted.
"Okay, okay, I'm done joking. I don't have any plans for the break, so I'm completely free. Are you going to the camp?"
"I'm still thinking about it. If you go, I'll go too. Are you going?"
"But Ongsa can't go."
"It's okay. You two can go. Don't worry about me."
"Our group won't feel complete if one of us is missing. Ask your mom first. It's only four days."
"All right... I'll try."

The stressful final exams were finally over. Today, the student council was heading to a volunteer camp in Ayutthaya. Everyone had to gather at school at five in the morning to arrive by late morning. Surprisingly, Ongsa's parents easily allowed her to go because they said, "She should get out more and explore the world."
"Good morning, Uncle. Oh my God, Ongsa, you look terrible. Did you have to drag her out of bed?"
"Something like that, Tinh. I'm leaving Ongsa in your hands. Don't let her fall asleep while standing."
"Yes, Uncle. We'll keep an eye on her. If she falls asleep, I'll smack her awake with my slipper. Don't worry."
Listen to Tinh, acting like the most devoted friend in the world.
As soon as Ongsa's father left, she tossed her backpack onto the table and slumped down to continue sleeping.
"I'm so sleepy..." Ongsa mumbled, barely able to keep her eyes open.
"Ongsa... Who could possibly wake you up right now?" Tinh asked.
"Tiffany Hwang, Girls' Generation," Ongsa answered sleepily, naming her favorite singer.
"I think this person could wake you up even faster than Tiffany. Turn around and look."
Charoen and Ongsa turned to look in the direction Tinh pointed.
"Sunny!" Charoen exclaimed in surprise when she saw Sun walking toward them with a backpack.
"It's Sun. Sunny's got bigger boobs."
"Tinh, you pervert!!!"

235_chapter3_content.text: This is Ongsa's first time participating in this kind of volunteer camp, so everything feels new to her. Beforehand, Pai, one of the staff members, told everyone that they had accepted a lot of campers this year because there were so many tasks to handle. And she wasn't kidding. As soon as they arrive in Ayutthaya, Ongsa's vision practically blurs from the sea of people.
“Tinh, Tinh, have you put your luggage away?”
“Yes. What's up, Pai?”
“Help me hand out the camp notebooks to everyone.”
“Oh, sure. Ongsa, Charoen, have you put your luggage away? Let's help hand out the notebooks.”

Ongsa can't help smiling when she hears that. This is her chance to hand Sun a notebook herself! Except... she fails. Sun goes to the restroom, and one of her friends takes the notebook for her instead. Another failure.

Did Ongsa somehow jinx herself before leaving home, condemning herself to one failure after another? Even though they're both here, she hasn't had a single chance to work with Sun. It's not that surprising, really. Someone as outgoing as Sun and someone as timid as Ongsa were never likely to end up working together.
Throughout the four days at camp, Ongsa keeps failing over and over again. This isn't just an ordinary losing streak. It's downright ridiculous.

Finally, it's the last night of camp. Before bedtime, everyone's having a party, something like a campfire night for middle schoolers. The staff have prepared performances to reward the campers for giving up four days of their time to do volunteer work.
“Next, the youngest member of our team will perform for you. Please give Sun a big round of applauseeee!”

Ongsa's head shoots up from her phone the moment she hears Pai, the host, announce Sun's name. The crowd claps and cheers as the pretty girl of the camp steps onto the stage. Ongsa is right there among them.
“What are you going to perform for us today, Sun?” Pai asks, holding the microphone out to her.

“I'm going to sing.” Sun flashes a smile that melts half the boys' hearts before continuing, “I actually had a guitarist when I rehearsed, but my friend had something urgent come up and couldn't make it. Does anyone here know how to play the guitar...?”
At that, everyone looks around at one another. Quite a few people raise their hands, but Ongsa is surprised to see that someone sitting right beside her has raised a hand, too.
“Charoen, it is!” Pai announces, choosing her.
Charoen gets up to collect the guitar and the chord sheet, then sits beside Sun. Her two best friends exchange bewildered looks.
“Charoen, you know how to play the guitar, Ongsa? How come I never knew?”
“I don't know either,” Ongsa answers.
“All right! Since you're ready, it's time for Sun and Charoen's performanceeee!”
Everyone claps.
“Okay. One, two, three, let's go!” Charoen counts them in and starts strumming.
“Why do you always smile whenever we cross paths?
Why does every word you say sound so sweet?
Why do you look so pleased whenever I look into your eyes?
I'm going... crazy... ♫”
Sun sings along to the guitar in her sweet voice.
She's already so cute. Does she really have to sing this well, too?
...Ongsa wonders.
“♪... ♫... It's like you've cast a spell that weakens my heart.
Do you know someone's getting all flustered?
I'm such a sucker for someone like you. I keep daydreaming, unable to eat or sleep.
I want to tell you just once. Please, I'm begging you.
Could you stop being so cute? My heart is melting. Oh, whoa, whoa...
Someone who looks like me should know their place.
I keep it all inside, even though my heart is racing.
I wouldn't dare ask an angel to fall for someone as humble as me.
It's like you've cast a spell that weakens my heart.
Do you know someone's getting all flustered?
I'm such a sucker for someone like you. I keep daydreaming, unable to eat or sleep.
I want to tell you just once. Please, I'm begging you.
Could you stop being so cute? My heart is melting. Oh, whoa, whoa...
What should I do with my heart? What should I do with this love?
You make me overthink everything. Honestly, I've completely lost to you.
My heart screams that I like you, but whenever I see you, I just stand there, confused.
What can I do to get over this? I've fallen for you... with all my heart... ♫... ♪”
Song: “แพ้ทาง” by LABANOON
...Ongsa thinks Sun shouldn't be singing this song...
...Ongsa should be the one singing it...
...Every single line hits her right in the feels...
“You're even recording her. How shameless...” someone sitting next to Ongsa teases.
“I'm filming Charoen,” Ongsa says quickly, trying to save herself after getting caught.
“Right... filming your friend, huh? Only half of Charoen's face is in the frame. She looks like a ghost. Do you think I'm an idiot, Miss Ongsa?”
Unable to argue back, Ongsa stays silent.
“Hey, can I sing, too?” Charoen suddenly asks, making everyone look at one another in confusion, especially her two best friends. They have absolutely no idea what she's up to.
“Charoen... you want to sing?” Pai asks to make sure.
“Yes,” Charoen answers confidently, stirring up the crowd with her unexpected announcement.
“Okay, go ahead!”
“Can you hold the microphone for me? I'll play the guitar,” Charoen asks Sun.
“Sure!” Sun replies, moving her chair closer so she can hold the microphone for Charoen.
“Hello, campers. Since I'm playing the guitar, I might as well perform a song,” Charoen says, strumming the strings like a professional.
“♫... ♪... I've brought my heart for you to consider... ♫”
...The very first line leaves the entire camp stunned...
“♫... ♪... Take a look at my heart and you'll know whether it's new or old.
Whether it's broken or damaged in some places,

“I don't have a type. My heart will tell me who the right person is.”
“Woooooooooooooooow!” Her answer gets the crowd going again.

“The kind of person I like talking to...? I like someone masculine, someone honest and straightforward. Someone reasonable, because I'm pretty irrational. Haha. I also prefer someone who's compatible with me. I can't really explain what that means. I'll know once I talk to them.”

“The Skytrain.”

...The camp notebook...

...Maybe...

...Tinh...
...Charoen...
“Fuck T^T”
Ongsa throws the notebook away without caring where it lands. What a perfect way to wrap up her epic tale of failure. These failures are heartbreakingly out of this world.

After spending her days taking it easy, going to cram school and resting, Ongsa's comfortable little school-break life comes to an end. The day before school starts, she tidies up her messy room to welcome the new semester and bring herself some good luck.

...The camp notebook...

“Names and numbers of camp staff:
First aiders:
Sun, Grade 10, Class 6”

“Ah... Oh, oh, it's a cockroach!”

What should she do now that she has Sun's number? Call her? No... Ongsa would never be brave enough. The hopelessly foolish Ongsa can only add Sun on LINE. Half a day has passed, but she still can't work up the courage to text her.
“Hi, I'm Ongsa...”
“No. I don't even know if she remembers me.”
“Hey... school's about to start. Are you excited?”
“That makes it sound like I know way too much about her. Delete.”
“What are you doing...?”
“Would I sound nosy? Nope, not this one.”

“This one, then.”
“Goodnight.”
Sent...
One minute later.
Five minutes later.
Thirty minutes later.
Two hours later.

It's normal not to reply to strangers.
Goodnight :-O

Goodnight :-O

Ongsa practically turns the house upside down looking for her phone, but she can't find it. If she were a drug addict, she'd be going through withdrawal by now. It's been three days since she lost it. Nothing is more torturous for a social media addict like Ongsa.

Staring at the Samsung Hero in her hand, Ongsa feels like crying. Her father gave it to her to use while she waits for a new phone. All she can do is turn the flashlight on and off. The SIM card isn't a problem; she bought one at a convenience store on the main road for the time being. It's not as if anyone is going to call her anyway.

A week later, Ongsa and her new Korean friend, the Samsung Hero, have started getting along. She's not sure whether her parents are really as busy as they claim or whether they're trying to teach her a lesson for not taking care of her belongings. They still haven't taken her to buy a new phone.
It's okay. Ongsa doesn't even feel anything anymore. TOT

“Okay, Mom.”

“Woof!”

“Woof!!”

...Her phone...

Ongsa picks it up to check all the notifications she's missed during the week she was without it, and then she spots a LINE message.
